paras: The attempted lynching of a waiter at Mont Eagle was a night attack in early August 1881 in which a mob of a dozen or more young men broke into the quarters of the Black waiters at a hotel in Mont Eagle, Tennessee, to lynch one of them. The waiter escaped when he was locked in a hotel room, and the mob's members were arrested and released on their promises not to repeat the act. The Memphis Public Ledger reported it as a "genuine sensation" under the headline "A colored Waiter That Barely Escaped Lynching."

A hotel at Mont Eagle employed twenty-five or thirty Black waiters, who lived in their own quarters. One of them was accused of throwing a plate at a pantry maid, described as "a white girl" whose home was in Nashville.

According to the Mont Eagle correspondent, "a dozen or more young mountaineers" heard of the incident and organized themselves into a mob to lynch the waiter. Between midnight and daylight they forced their way into the waiters' quarters and demanded the accused man. The demand set off a panic, and the other waiters fled into the brush. The accused waiter went to the hotel, where he was locked in a room to keep the mob from reaching him.

The waiter was afterward arraigned before the Recorder and fined $15.50. Every member of the mob was arrested and taken before a magistrate, and each was released on his individual promise never to do the like again. The waiter was then put on a train at night and sent to Nashville. No names of the waiter, the maid or the mob's members appear in the coverage.

The only report found is a letter dated August 8 from a Mont Eagle correspondent signed "J. C. C.," printed on page 4 of the Memphis Public Ledger on August 9, 1881. Its tone was light and mock-formal, calling the waiter "the sable dispenser of viands" and "the refactory individual," and it called him "the guilty waiter" before he had been tried.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of a waiter at Mont Eagle
bases: A mob of a dozen or more 'organized themselves into a mob for the purpose of lynching' a Black waiter and forced their way into the waiters' quarters to seize him, but he escaped (A1).
A group of a dozen or more acting without authority sought to lynch the waiter over an accusation, but he was hidden in the hotel and no one was killed, so this was an attempted lynching (A1).
The only report found is one correspondent's letter in the Memphis Public Ledger (A1); no other paper in the window carried it.

accounts.label: Mont Eagle correspondent
accounts.gist: A dozen or more young mountaineers formed a mob to lynch a colored waiter who threw a plate at a white pantry maid, broke into the waiters' quarters, and failed to reach him; the mob was arrested and released on promises, and the waiter was fined and sent to Nashville.

framing.detail: Treated the affair as a 'genuine sensation' told in a jocular register ('sable dispenser of viands'), stated the plate-throwing as fact and called the waiter 'guilty', while noting the mob's arrest without comment.
